newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to free car insurance rates in 98/99--paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan to free car insurance rates in 98/99--paper.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry plans to deregulate rates for car and fire insurance in fiscal 1998/99, Japanese media reported on Wednesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun financial daily said the plan is expected to help facilitate an agreement in ongoing Japan-U.S. insurance talks.
The timing of the liberalisation of Japan's system of setting car insurance premiums has been one of the major sticking points in their bilateral insurance dispute.

Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka are expected to meet in Tokyo on Saturday in a last-ditch effort to resolve the insurance dispute by a December 15 deadline.

Currently, an independent body calculates premium rates which all non-life insurance firms are obliged to adopt. Washington has called on Japan to completely liberalise the system as soon as possible.

Japanese non-life insurance companies have expressed strong concern over the liberalisation of premiums, saying it could lead to higher rates for young people who are more prone to accidents and result in an increase in the number of drivers without insurance coverage.
A Finance Ministry official declined to comment on the report.
